data.title: Tranexamic acid + Peptides + Niacinamide (e.g. Melanotx-type serum)
data.summary: VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting · Combination depigmenting cosmeceutical (topical tranexamic acid–based)
data.body:
_Topicals · VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting_

**Class:** Combination depigmenting cosmeceutical (topical tranexamic acid–based)

## Mechanism of action
- Tranexamic acid (lysine analogue, 2–5%): inhibits plasminogen → plasmin conversion in keratinocytes → less arachidonic acid, prostaglandins and α-MSH → less melanocyte stimulation; also reduces dermal vascularity in melasma
- Niacinamide (2–5%): blocks transfer of melanosomes from melanocytes to keratinocytes; improves barrier
- Peptides (e.g. oligopeptide-68, nonapeptide-1): block MITF/α-MSH signalling → reduce melanin synthesis

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Melasma (adjunct, maintenance), PIH
- Oral tranexamic acid (250 mg twice daily) is more effective for melasma, but is a systemic drug (thrombosis risk)

## Dose & formulations
- Once or twice daily with daytime sunscreen; assess at 8–12 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Mild irritation, dryness, erythema

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Topical TXA and niacinamide are considered low risk; limited data.

## Viva points
- Topical TXA works on the plasmin–prostaglandin pathway and vascular component of melasma
- Niacinamide blocks melanosome transfer — not tyrosinase

## Note on sources
The exam list's brand name ('Melanotx Ultra') could not be confirmed; the post covers the ingredient combination.

_Sources: Khopkar ch.26 and ch.29 (niacinamide); published melasma trials; product information. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
